summary: Implemented ArrTags-side provider inventory cache invalidation (ADR-018 clause 3). ArrInventoryCache gained a bounded, thread-safe Invalidate(ArrConnectionId)/InvalidateAll() surface that removes retained observation sets under the same gate as TryStore/TryGet (no lock held across provider I/O, safe concurrently with reads and populations); ArrInventoryCacheProvider exposes the same surface against the cache resolved from the current configuration snapshot. An accepted provider webhook (ADR-012) invalidates the event's provider/connection from the hosted WebhookIntakeService loop before any hint is enqueued (bounded invalidate-all when the connection cannot be resolved), never blocking or throwing into the Jellyfin request. Jellyfin library refresh/post-scan, manual and periodic scheduled, and post-save reconciliation all invalidate at the start of LibraryReconciliationService.ReconcileAsync so their work begins a fresh provider-read window; the periodic scheduled reconciliation keeps its unchanged 12-hour default interval and still enqueues work (v1.1 is not refresh-only). The bounded TTL fallback remains in TryGet. No provider conditional request, ETag/If-None-Match, revision token, history/since watermark, or SignalR dependency was added; the invalidation API carries only the non-secret connection identifier. The in-flight population interaction is documented: a population that completes after an invalidation may store the read it took before it, bounded by the configured TTL and repaired by the next webhook/refresh/scheduled/manual reconciliation.

known_limitations: In-flight population interaction: a single-flight population already in flight when an invalidation runs may complete afterwards and store the provider read it took before the invalidation. Consequence: that observation set can be served until its configured inventory TTL (StaleUntil), and it is discarded by the next webhook, refresh/post-scan, or scheduled/manual reconciliation; the cache is non-authoritative so correctness does not depend on it. This is the bounded behavior the task asked to document rather than fence with a generation counter.

Reconciliation invalidation runs after the no-enabled-provider and lifecycle-fence guards in ReconcileAsync, so a run that is skipped for no enabled provider or a raised fence does not invalidate. Consequence: no observation set is discarded for a run that enqueues no work; the next actual reconciliation, webhook, or the TTL still invalidates.

Webhook connection resolution uses ArrConnectionCatalog.FromSnapshot(current snapshot) by provider kind; because the catalog always returns both provider connections, the bounded invalidate-all fallback is defensive and is not exercised by the current catalog shape.

Limitation F1 is deliberately not recorded as resolved by this task; task 11.4 records it resolved after the Goal C integration verification. The live pinned-host verification of this behavior remains owned by task 14.3 per the project plan.
